9.text: Nvidia authorized a record $150 billion stock buyback after posting over 100% revenue growth, with CEO Jensen Huang citing a once-in-a-generation AI platform shift. Analysts upgraded the stock, noting its forward earnings multiple has fallen to a decade low despite surging profits.

10.text: Micron guided to an 86% gross margin ahead of Wednesday's earnings, with Wall Street raising targets on higher memory prices and AI demand; Sandisk jumped 22% after Micron's last report. Articles compare Micron and Sandisk as AI memory winners while flagging cyclical risks, and note diversified ETFs as alternatives to betting on Micron alone.

6.text: Broadcom projects AI revenue of $58B in fiscal 2026 and $230B by fiscal 2028, with analysts debating whether its stock, Marvell, AMD, or Intel offers the better AI-chip buy. Nvidia is mentioned mainly as the incumbent these rivals are chasing.

11.text: Nebius will raise GPU cloud prices 20% on Oct. 1 after a capacity auction cleared above projections, and BNP Paribas upgraded the stock to $399, sending shares up. CoreWeave reported scaling margins, a $104B backlog, raised 2026 revenue guidance, and strong demand with price increases.

12.text: Michael Burry replaced his Nvidia, Micron, and Palantir short positions with put options, betting the AI bubble could burst sooner than later. He also warned that AI revenue is dangerously concentrated and that hyperscalers carry $3 trillion in off-balance-sheet obligations.

7.text: Chip stocks rebounded after a two-day decline, with the iShares Semiconductor ETF hitting its highest close since June. SK Hynix’s Solidigm is weighing an IPO that could raise $15 billion, while China’s influence on chip demand is fading.
